classification.difficultyReason: Identify an order-sensitive horizontal reflection and translation, then transform a qualitative curve and its key features.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows $y=f(x)$.
First describe the transformations in $y=f(1-x)$ and sketch the new curve.

spec.sourceRegion: Upper question, supplied graph beneath question 16
spec.description: Editable qualitative decreasing curve with upper-left and downward continuation arrows, crossing the x-axis at −1 and approaching the y-axis from the left. No formula, grid or additional numerical scale is introduced. Source blue is replaced by ordinary black because this figure has only one series.
spec.mathematics: The curve has x-intercept (−1,0), lies in x<0, and approaches the vertical asymptote x=0 from the left. Bezier controls describe qualitative shape only, not additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible in the student edition; no transformed curve is included.

answer.short: Reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate 1 unit right. Alternatively, translate 1 unit left, then reflect in the $y$-axis. The new curve crosses at $(2,0)$ and approaches $x=1$ from the right.
answer.worked:
$$y=f\bigl(-(x-1)\bigr).$$
Reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate 1 unit right. Alternatively, translate 1 unit left, then reflect in the $y$-axis.
Each point $(x,y)$ maps to $(1-x,y)$, so $(-1,0)$ maps to $(2,0)$ and the vertical asymptote $x=0$ maps to $x=1$. Sketch the increasing curve to the right of $x=1$, approaching that line downwards and continuing upwards to the right.

spec.description: Complete solution graph using exactly the supplied graph's Bezier path under the affine transformation x↦1−x. The dashed line identifies the transformed vertical asymptote.
spec.mathematics: Every point and Bezier control point maps by (x,y)↦(1−x,y). The image is increasing on x>1, crosses the x-axis at 2, and approaches x=1 from the right downwards.
